title: Japa Yoga: A Comprehensive Treatise on Mantra-Sastra
author: Swami Sivananda
year: undated on page (first ed. c. 1930s-40s; not verified)
edition_cited: Divine Life Society web edition, ISBN 81-7052-018-5
locator_hints: Introduction, Part III: gaze-then-close visualisation of Ishta-Devata; light in the heart; ignore coloured lights
summary: Sivananda's treatise on mantra. The web page (introduction only; PDF fetch failed) has no claim that japa itself produces seen light and no first-person report. It gives an open-eye/closed-eye alternation for building the image of the Ishta-Devata (gaze at a picture a few minutes, close eyes, reopen when it fades, 5-6 rounds, clear after months), a fallback of fixing the mind on the effulgent light in the heart, and the instruction to ignore visions and coloured lights in silent meditation.
why_relevant: Gaze-and-close alternation is a borderline afterimage/visualisation method; the warning to ignore coloured lights counts. Direct japa-light linkage not found.

date_evidence.basis: No publication year on the dlshq.org book page; only site footer copyright 2026. Author died 1963, so text certainly pre-2023, but the page itself is undated.
